sourceInformation.source: the complete summer and winter Olympic games
sourceInformation.perspective: 2.5D lanes (brawler view) for the 100m Dash, side view for the Ski Jump, overhead view for Archery
sourceInformation.tech: my-3D2dge v0.85.2 handoff engine (copy, unchanged), plain JavaScript on canvas; Node 24 for headless tests; Python Playwright with Chromium for screenshots
sourceInformation.artDirection: Engine pixel style: chibi Humanoid rigs, sky gradients, flat track and ramp shapes, a code-drawn archery target
sourceInformation.animation: Engine Humanoid rig poses (run, air, down) driven each step
sourceInformation.audio: Engine chip synth, sound presets and song loops (E.songs); no audio files; no voices
sourceInformation.testing: Headless scripted playthroughs (21 checks, one command) and browser screenshots
sourceInformation.research: The engine's own docs only (API card, README, API index); no web research
sourceInformation.environment: Claude Code CLI (headless); Linux (WSL2); Chromium via Playwright for screenshots

testingFeedback: Six game bugs. Two were critical: attract mode never returned to the title, and the tracks, ramp and archery target drew nothing. Four were smaller: the ski camera sat under the hill, unsupported glyphs showed as '?', the results screen read a stale global during a fade, and the medal table compared random numbers with times.
The scripted Quick Games run, from the title through the medal table, because it crosses every scene change and checks that nine medals were handed out.
The scene-name checks. They passed while the track was blank; only the screenshots caught that.
engineFeedback: The scene and pause-menu setup, and the headless fixed-step advance, which made the tests repeatable.

Yes, twice. E.hex returns arrays that the pixel helpers reject, so the colours silently drew nothing. Scene fades also swallow input, so scripted tests need a wait after every scene change. The font lacks the middle dot and the controller symbols.
The three event simulations, the attract pilot, the dev sliders and the About screens.
Knowing which draw calls are screen space: r.overlay paints over the actors, so ground shapes have to go in r.decal or r.queue.
None. The engine copy is unchanged.
Add the controller symbols and the middle dot to the pixel font, and say in the API card which colour format each draw call takes.
promptFeedback: The 10-foot rules, and the exact file names and deliverable list.
The plan is 1700 lines written for a team at max effort, names an Opus folder, and the root folder is not stated clearly: STAGE says root, the plan says beside TASK.md.
Fitting twelve events, AI Hub, ceremonies and voices into one session. I built three events and stopped there.
Mark a first-pass scope by priority, name the root folder, and trim the plan to what one session can build, keeping the done checklist the same.

aiHub.name: Olympiyikes!
aiHub.description: A playful arcade riff on the Summer and Winter Games: mash, time and aim through three events, then check the Quick Games medal table.
aiHub.controls: Mash J and K, Space to act, L for turbo, arrows to balance and nudge (pad: square and circle mash, cross acts, triangle turbo)
